title: Public-Private Partnerships and Financial Intelligence Sharing
summary: A six-module programme equipping FIUs and law-enforcement agencies to design, run and evaluate public-private partnerships for sharing financial intelligence lawfully and effectively.
intro: This training programme equips FIUs and law-enforcement agencies to design, run and evaluate public-private partnerships for sharing financial intelligence, within clear legal gateways and data protection safeguards.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give FIU and law-enforcement managers a practical understanding of how financial information-sharing partnerships work and what makes them effective. Participants leave able to choose an appropriate partnership model, put lawful gateways and safeguards in place, run tactical and strategic sharing, and measure and demonstrate results.
sections.What It Covers: The case for public-private partnerships, partnership models and governance, legal gateways for sharing, data protection and confidentiality safeguards, tactical and strategic information sharing, private-to-private sharing and collaborative analytics, and measuring results.
Intended Audience: FIU heads, partnership managers and senior analysts
Law-enforcement leads for economic crime, fraud and terrorist financing
Policy, legal and data protection officers advising on information-sharing arrangements
Learning Objectives: Explain the purposes and benefits of public-private financial information sharing
Compare partnership models and choose one suited to the national framework
Identify the legal gateways that permit sharing and the limits they impose
Apply data protection, confidentiality and tipping-off safeguards
Run tactical and strategic sharing that produces actionable results
Measure and demonstrate the partnership's outcomes and value
sections.Structure and Format: Six modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing with case studies of partnership models and design exercises, ending in a partnership planning workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the national legal framework.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial intelligence, investigation or AML/CFT policy is helpful. No legal or data protection expertise is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2017), Guidance on Private Sector Information Sharing
FATF (2021), Stocktake on Data Pooling, Collaborative Analytics and Data Protection
FATF (2022), Partnering in the Fight Against Financial Crime: Data Protection, Technology and Private Sector Information Sharing
Egmont Group (2013), Principles for Information Exchange Between Financial Intelligence Units

modules.title: The Case for Public-Private Partnerships
modules.summary: Why one-way reporting alone is not enough, what public-private partnerships add to financial intelligence, and what FATF work and international experience say about their effectiveness.
objectives: Explain the limits of one-way suspicious transaction reporting
Describe the benefits and risks of public-private partnerships
Summarise FATF work on private sector information sharing
syllabus: From one-way reporting to two-way sharing
Benefits: better targeting, faster response and improved reporting
Risks: legal exposure, de-risking and unequal participation
FATF guidance and international experience

modules.title: Partnership Models and Governance
modules.summary: The main models of public-private partnership, from strategic forums to tactical taskforces, and the governance, membership and trust arrangements that make them sustainable.
objectives: Compare strategic, tactical and hybrid partnership models
Design governance, membership and terms of reference
Build trust and manage expectations between partners
syllabus: Strategic forums, tactical taskforces and hybrid models
Membership: banks, payment firms, crypto-asset providers and others
Terms of reference, chairing and decision-making
Vetting, security and building trust

modules.title: Legal Gateways and Data Protection
modules.summary: The legal bases that permit sharing between authorities and firms and between firms, and how to embed data protection, confidentiality and tipping-off safeguards from the outset.
objectives: Identify the legal gateways for public-to-private and private-to-private sharing
Apply data protection principles, including necessity and proportionality
Manage confidentiality, tipping-off and liability risks
syllabus: Statutory gateways, safe harbours and information-sharing provisions
Data protection principles and impact assessments
Confidentiality, tipping-off and protection from liability
Privacy-enhancing technologies and collaborative analytics

modules.title: Tactical and Strategic Sharing in Practice
modules.summary: How partnerships share information on specific cases and subjects and on threats and typologies, and how outputs feed investigations, reporting and firms' controls.
objectives: Run tactical sharing on live cases securely and lawfully
Produce strategic threat and typology products with partners
Turn shared intelligence into investigative and preventive action
syllabus: Tactical sharing: requests, responses and targeted reporting
Strategic sharing: threat assessments, typologies and alerts
Handling, dissemination and onward use of shared information
Feeding results into investigations and firms' monitoring

modules.title: Measuring Results and Demonstrating Value
modules.summary: How to measure the outputs, outcomes and wider impact of a partnership, avoid vanity metrics, and report results credibly to government, partners and assessors.
objectives: Define meaningful measures of partnership performance
Collect and attribute results across agencies and firms
Report outcomes credibly, including to mutual evaluation assessors
syllabus: Outputs, outcomes and impact: what to measure
Attributing arrests, freezes and reporting improvements
Qualitative evidence and case studies
Reporting to government, partners and assessors

modules.title: Designing a Partnership: Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a workshop in which teams design or improve a partnership for their own context, covering model, legal basis, safeguards, priorities and measures.
objectives: Apply the programme to design or reform a partnership
Identify legal and practical obstacles and how to address them
Produce a partnership plan with priorities and measures
syllabus: Assessing the current information-sharing landscape
Choosing the model, members and priority threats
Legal, data protection and governance checklist
Workshop: the partnership design and twelve-month plan

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.

related.title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.

related.title: Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime Investigations
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud, money mules and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to recover funds.

related.title: Prosecuting Financial Crime: Evidence, Experts and the Courtroom
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases, from charge and evidence to sentencing and confiscation.

related.title: Tax Crime and Money Laundering
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping tax, FIU and law-enforcement investigators to tackle tax crime and related laundering through information exchange and joint investigation.
